summary: The note examines the growing problem of electronic waste driven by frequent device upgrades, and how electronics manufacturers are responding. It covers e-waste statistics, manufacturer take-back programs, design for recycling, Extended Producer Responsibility, international standards, consumer education, and emerging recycling technologies such as organic solvents and mycelium-based insulation.
one_line: Overview of the global e-waste problem and how manufacturers, policy (EPR), education and new technologies are addressing it.
key_facts: TechTrend launched its newest smartphone in September 2023, which left a growing pile of discarded older models in its wake.

John Smith, an environmental analyst at Green Solutions, said on October 15, 2023: "Every year, millions of gadgets are replaced and abandoned, leading to a dire need for robust e-waste management solutions."
A Global EWaste Monitor study released on September 10, 2023 found the world generated 53.6 million metric tons of electronic waste in the previous year.
Only 17.4% of that e-waste was formally collected and recycled; the rest often ends up in landfills or is dumped in developing countries, releasing lead, mercury, and cadmium.
Jane Doe, CEO of EcoElectro, announced on November 1, 2023 a program aiming to recover and recycle 70% of the products the company has sold by 2025.
RecoElec has invested in a modular phone design that simplifies repair, upgrades, and recycling.
As of December 2023, the industry lacks widespread adherence to design-for-disassembly principles, citing cost-effectiveness and market competition.
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) makes producers responsible for the end-of-life treatment of electronics as well as their manufacture.
Dr. Maria Hernandez, an environmental policy expert, said on January 5, 2024 that EPR policies have the potential to dramatically reduce e-waste.
The Basel Convention aims to prevent transfer of hazardous waste between nations, but compliance varies and illegal trade persists.
TechTrend launched an educational initiative on January 20, 2024 to boost e-waste recycling awareness among its customers.
CleanCircuit is developing an organic solvent to decompose circuit boards into non-toxic compounds, set to be commercialized by 2026.
On March 11, 2024, MycoTech and EcoElectro announced a biodegradable wiring insulation made from mycelium, a form of fungus.
